name: WebGPU compute
plain: Lets a page run general GPU compute shaders.
meaning: Used for local AI and rendering. Reveals GPU class and limits.

access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

limits.headline: Can use your graphics chip for heavy math, and learn what kind of chip you have
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when a page loads a game, an AI feature or a 3D view
can: Run AI models and 3D graphics on your graphics chip
Learn the rough class and limits of your chip
Run mining scripts that use your chip, which is an abuse
cannot: See your files or other apps
Work in Firefox on most computers yet

limits.differs: Chrome, Edge and Safari support it, including iPhone. Firefox support is partial.

story.what_it_is: A page can use your graphics chip for heavy math, not only for pictures.

marketing.name: WebGPU API
marketing.pitch: Gives web apps modern, fast access to the graphics chip for rich 3D, and general computing.

story.for_you: You never see a prompt. Heavy pages feel faster and games look better. Your fan may spin up, and the page may use more battery.
story.for_makers: Makers use the GPU for 3D games, video effects, photo editing and running AI models in the page. It makes web apps rival desktop ones. It also exposes details of your graphics chip, which adds to a fingerprint, and can be abused for hidden mining.

use_cases.example: A browser 3D game uses compute shaders for physics and crowds, so thousands of units move smoothly in a tab.
A browser video editor applies filters and effects to 4K clips using the graphics chip.
A web design or photo tool uses it for blur, filters and live preview.
A page runs a small AI model for image search directly in the browser with GPU speed.
A cloud gaming or video call page runs background blur and upscaling on the GPU.
A web data tool draws millions of points in a chart using GPU math.
A tracking script reads the GPU name and speed to add to a device fingerprint.
A hidden crypto mining script uses the GPU on a hacked site.
